risk_if_not_implemented: Without Resource Exhaustion & Denial of Service (DoS) Resilience, critical business processes and services may not withstand or recover from disruption, causing extended outages and data loss. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Business / Service Interruption (R-BC-1), Undetected / Delayed Detection of Adverse Activity (R-SA-1), Loss of Data / Service Availability (R-IP-4), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Artificial Intelligence & Autonomous Technologies (AAT) System Failure or Unintended Behavior (MT-13), Adversarial Artificial Intelligence (AI) Attack (MT-29).

compensating_control_1.name: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS)
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to operate a Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) to achieve resilient Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) during:
(1) Routine operations; and
(2) Adverse conditions.
compensating_control_1.justification: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) (BCD-02) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Resource Exhaustion & DoS Resilience (AAT-38.3) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Data Backups
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to create recurring backups of data, software and/or system images, as well as verify the integrity of these backups, to ensure the availability of the data to satisfy Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs).
compensating_control_2.justification: Data Backups (BCD-24) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Resource Exhaustion & DoS Resilience (AAT-38.3) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
